purpose: Constrain post-enrollment semantic authoring so no primary RISU result can influence unit order, source consequence declaration, evidence-strength classification, target-model repair, or retention.
order_rule: Primary authoring and primary verifier execution proceed in enrollment order. A blocked or incomplete unit remains in place; later units may proceed only after the earlier unit has either an AUTHOR_ACCEPTED freeze or a committed AUTHORING_BLOCKED record explaining the unresolved evidence boundary.

SOURCE.goal: Reconstruct the source operation's consequence-defining version distinction independently of the target projection result.
required_outputs: source operation identity and immutable evidence references
reviewed or otherwise authoritative version coordinate
current version coordinate observable at the declared effect cut
forbidden: using a target omission or target implementation quirk to invent the source consequence
strengthening documentation evidence into live-runtime conformance
selecting a source semantic because it makes the target fail

TARGET.goal: Reconstruct only what the pinned target actually exposes and executes, without importing the desired source consequence into missing target facts.
required_outputs: implementation path or generated binding path
forbidden: assuming an omitted guard exists because the source API supports it
treating documentation wording as operative placement unless implementation or equivalent evidence establishes it
repairing the target model after observing a primary RISU result without a numbered authoring amendment

merge_gate.rule: SOURCE and TARGET lanes are merged into a VBE instance only after both lane records are frozen for the unit.
required_checks: carrier facts remain distinct from semantic interpretation
all unresolved uncertainty either narrows the claim or blocks author acceptance

record_must_state: evidence references were checked against pinned identities
source consequence was not chosen from the target result
target facts were not inferred solely from desired semantics
bounded worlds and effect cut are accepted
remaining uncertainty and evidence limits are listed
no RISU primary verdict for this unit has been observed

uncertainty_policy.rule: Uncertainty is not a defect to hide. If a material source or target fact cannot be established at the declared evidence strength, narrow the claim or commit AUTHORING_BLOCKED / INCOMPLETE_ASSURANCE rather than filling the gap by interpretation.
uncertainty_policy.prohibited: Do not create evidence facts merely to fit one of the existing compiler patterns.

evidence_rule: Every material statement records the strongest layer actually supported. A higher layer may depend on lower layers, but no lower-layer observation is relabeled as a stronger layer without an explicit derivation record.

issue_tracker_policy.rule: Any post-result issue or bug evidence is reported separately and cannot alter enrollment or retroactively strengthen the primary pre-result evidence record.

allowed: live-runtime experiment if separately scoped and labeled
diagnostics_after_primary_result.rule: Diagnostics are secondary records. They do not rewrite the primary AUTHOR_ACCEPTED input or primary verdict.

friction_measurement.stop: primary result freeze for the unit
friction_measurement.automation_decision_rule: Do not redesign the product from a single unit. Aggregate repeated friction across units before promoting a manual step into a compiler or extractor feature.

historical_overlap_policy.unit_001: The older GitHub merge case is disclosure context only. Its old result may not be used to author the current revision's source or target facts. The current pinned target revision must be reconstructed independently.
historical_overlap_policy.general: Prior RISU cases may identify reusable evidence schemas or tooling, but a prior verdict may not substitute for current-revision evidence.

change_control: No in-place changes after the first unit SOURCE lane begins. Any correction requires AUTHORING_PROTOCOL_AMENDMENT_NNN with timing, affected rule, reason, whether any primary verdict had been observed, and whether the correction could alter a primary outcome.
